adc-dac-030.summary: JA explanation says Nyquist-rate ADCs sample at 'about twice the Nyquist frequency'. adc-dac-030.basis: Nyquist frequency = fs/2, so fs = 2 x Nyquist frequency holds for any converter, including ΔΣ. The distinction is fs ≈ 2 x signal bandwidth (Nyquist rate) vs fs >> 2 x bandwidth. EN correctly says 'about twice the signal bandwidth', so JA and EN also differ.

gpu-programming-014.summary: Claims the strided a[i*32] access moves "tens of times" more data than a[i]. On current NVIDIA GPUs global memory is transferred in 32-byte sectors, so each thread pulls one 32-byte sector: 32x32 B = 1024 B vs 128 B, i.e. 8x. The 32x figure only holds for 128-byte transaction granularity.
gpu-programming-014.basis: a[i]: 32 threads x 4 B = 128 B = 4 sectors. a[i*32]: 32 distinct 128-B-apart addresses -> 32 sectors x 32 B = 1024 B (8x); with 128-B lines 4096 B (32x). Since Maxwell/Pascal, L2/DRAM access granularity is 32-B sectors (CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide, coalesced access section).

hdl-verification-027.summary: The explanation's fix is wrong for this code: it says declaring the signals 'wire signed [7:0]' makes the comparison give 0, but the other operand is 8'd1, a sized literal that is unsigned, so the expression stays unsigned and gt remains 1. It also refers to 'a and b' although the code has no b. The EN explanation repeats the wrong fix.
hdl-verification-027.basis: IEEE 1364-2005 / 1800: sized or based constants (e.g. 8'd1) are unsigned unless the 's' designator is used (8'sd1). If any operand of a relational expression is unsigned, the whole expression is evaluated as unsigned. So with 'wire signed [7:0] a = 8'hFF;', 'a > 8'd1' still compares 255 > 1 and gives 1; 'a > 8'sd1' (or the unsized signed literal 1) gives -1 > 1 = 0. The explanation itself states the 'one unsigned operand makes it all unsigned' rule, which contradicts its own fix.
hdl-verification-027.by: AI audit (reviewed by maintainer), not human expert review

hw-security-031.summary: The explanation says, without qualification, that processing a chip to read a PUF value changes the variation itself. That is a design goal of some PUFs, such as coating PUFs or PUFs with a tamper-sensitive layer, but not a general property. Researchers have read out and even cloned SRAM PUF start-up values by semi-invasive methods (photonic emission analysis plus FIB edits). (EN: same claim.)
hw-security-031.basis: Helfmeier, Boit, Nedospasov, Seifert, 'Cloning Physically Unclonable Functions' (HOST 2013) read out an SRAM PUF's start-up pattern through the chip backside and cloned it with FIB, so reading did not destroy the variation. Tamper-evidence holds only for some PUF types.
hw-security-031.by: AI audit (reviewed by maintainer), not human expert review

ion-implant-018.summary: Says resist must be "several times" the ion range (Rp + several ΔRp). The usual masking criterion is thickness >= Rp + m·ΔRp evaluated in the resist (m about 3-5); requiring several times that is not necessary and misstates the rule.
ion-implant-018.basis: Standard mask-thickness criterion (e.g., Plummer/Deal/Griffin, Silicon VLSI Technology): choose d so that the transmitted fraction (tail beyond d of the Gaussian in the mask material) is negligible, i.e., d = Rp + m·ΔRp with Rp, ΔRp for the mask material. The lower density of resist is already accounted for by using resist Rp (larger than in Si), not by a multiplier.

linker-loader-005.summary: For a C program, the explanation says a difference in arguments can turn the call into a different symbol name. C does not mangle names, so an argument/signature mismatch does not change the symbol (it links, with undefined behavior); only C++ name mangling does that. EN repeats it ('signature mismatch').
linker-loader-005.basis: C compilers emit the plain identifier (e.g. foo or _foo) regardless of parameter types; argument types are encoded only by C++ name mangling (cf. linker-loader-035 in the same category).

lithography-001.summary: R from the Rayleigh formula with k1=0.27 is a half-pitch (≈39 nm), but the text says 'pitches finer than this need multiple patterning or EUV', which implies a ~39 nm pitch limit. The single-exposure pitch limit is ~77–80 nm, as lithography-005 itself states ('ピッチ約80 nm').
lithography-001.basis: 0.27×193/1.35 = 38.6 nm = half-pitch; pitch = 2R ≈ 77 nm. k1=0.25 is the half-pitch limit (lithography-021), so R is a half-pitch. lithography-005 gives the ArF immersion pitch limit as about 80 nm, so 001 contradicts 005 by a factor of 2.

lithography-012.summary: Stage acceleration stated as 'a few m/s²' (数m/s²). Modern scanner stages accelerate an order of magnitude faster: tens of m/s² (several g) for the wafer stage, and more for the reticle stage.
lithography-012.basis: ASML's High-NA (EXE:5000) material gives wafer stage 8 g (~80 m/s²), twice the NXE wafer stage (~4 g ≈ 40 m/s²), and reticle stage 32 g. Even older scanner patents cite reticle accelerations of 0.5–4 G. So 'a few m/s²' (<1 g) is about 10x too low for current tools. Source: asml.com '5 things you should know about High NA EUV lithography' (2024).
lithography-012.by: AI audit (reviewed by maintainer), not human expert review

logic-038.summary: States that a JK flip-flop with J and K tied to 1 'is' a T flip-flop. A T flip-flop has a T input (T=0 hold, T=1 toggle) and is obtained by tying J and K together as the T input; fixing both at 1 only gives the always-toggle case. logic-039 itself uses 'T flip-flop (T = 1)', i.e. treats T as an input.
logic-038.basis: Standard definition: T-FF next state Q+ = T xor Q; JK with J=K=T gives Q+ = T·¬Q + ¬T·Q = T xor Q. J=K=1 fixed gives only Q+ = ¬Q.
logic-038.by: AI audit (reviewed by maintainer), not human expert review

physics-025.summary: States that 1–10 Ω·cm p-type wafers correspond to boron 'in the 10^15 cm^-3 range' (10¹⁵ cm⁻³ 台). By the standard resistivity–doping conversion (Irvin curves / ASTM F723), 10 Ω·cm p-type ≈ 1.3×10^15 cm^-3 but 1 Ω·cm p-type ≈ 1.5×10^16 cm^-3, so the span is 10^15–10^16 cm^-3.
physics-025.basis: Hole mobility ≈ 400–470 cm²/V·s at these dopings: N = 1/(qρμ) → ρ=10 Ω·cm: 1/(1.6e-19×10×470) ≈ 1.3e15; ρ=1 Ω·cm: 1/(1.6e-19×1×~410) ≈ 1.5e16 cm^-3. The 1 Ω·cm end falls outside the 10^15 decade.

lithography-016.summary: The explanation says photomask writers use an electron beam 'focused to a few nm' (数nmに細く絞った電子線). Production mask writers do not work this way.
lithography-016.basis: Production photomask writers are variable-shaped-beam (VSB) tools such as the NuFlare EBM series. They shape the beam into rectangles of variable size, up to sub-µm shots, and expose pattern by pattern. Multi-beam mask writers such as the IMS MBMW use beamlets of roughly 10-20 nm on a ~10 nm grid. A Gaussian beam focused to a few nm belongs to research and direct-write EBL tools (lithography-041), not the mainstream mask writer. The rest of the explanation (serial writing, >10 h per mask, multi-beam writers with hundreds of thousands of beamlets) is correct. The fix states the beam as focused or shaped and drops the 'few nm' figure. No numbers are added, so the number cross-check between languages is unaffected.

lithography-018.summary: The standing-wave parenthetical '縦方向の縞' is ambiguous in Japanese, and every translation renders it as 'vertical stripes' (en 'vertical ripples', de 'vertikale Streifen', fr 'stries verticales', nl 'verticale strepen', ko '세로 줄무늬', zh '縱向條紋'). That gets the orientation wrong.
lithography-018.basis: Incident light and light reflected from the substrate form a standing wave along the film normal, with intensity maxima and minima every λ/(2n) (about 57 nm for ArF in a resist with n≈1.7). The exposure therefore varies with depth, giving bright and dark layers parallel to the wafer. On the developed sidewalls these appear as horizontal ridges ('scalloping'), not as vertical stripes. The ja '縦方向の縞' is only correct if read as 'striped along the vertical direction', and the translations took it the other way. The fix rewords the parenthetical so it says the bright/dark pattern repeats through the depth, in all languages.

etching-035.summary: The explanation attributes the negative DC self-bias of a capacitively coupled electrode solely to electrons being more mobile than ions, and states it as holding for any such electrode. The condition that actually produces a nonzero DC self-bias, namely the powered (wafer) electrode being smaller in area than the grounded electrode/walls, is missing; without it the statement is false.
etching-035.basis: Electron/ion mobility difference makes every RF sheath rectifying, so each surface sits negative relative to the plasma on time average. The DC voltage that builds up across the blocking capacitor (the self-bias measured from ground) comes from the asymmetry of the two sheaths: by the Koenig-Maissel area relation V1/V2 = (A2/A1)^q (q ~ 1-4), the smaller electrode gets the larger sheath voltage. For a symmetric discharge (equal electrode areas) the DC self-bias is zero even though electrons are still far more mobile (Lieberman & Lichtenberg, Principles of Plasma Discharges and Materials Processing, ch. 11, capacitive discharges / asymmetric discharges). Real etchers have a small wafer electrode and large grounded chamber walls, so the keyed answer stays correct; only the mechanism sentence needs the missing condition.

eda-047.summary: The worked example says that with a 1 ns period and 50 ps uncertainty the data must arrive by 0.95 ns, leaving out the setup time of the capturing flip-flop. The de translation additionally says "nach 0,95 ns eintreffen" (arrive AFTER 0.95 ns), which reverses the meaning.
eda-047.basis: In STA the required time for a setup check is (period - clock uncertainty - setup time of the capture flip-flop), ignoring clock latencies. Clock uncertainty only reduces the usable window from 1 ns to 0.95 ns; the data must arrive earlier than 0.95 ns by the library setup time. Stating 0.95 ns as the arrival deadline misidentifies the quantity. This matches the glossary entry クロックの不確かさ (margin subtracted from the usable time). In de, "nach 0,95 ns" means "after 0.95 ns"; the ja/en/nl/fr say "within/by".

mosfet-022.summary: 解説が「厚さ0.3〜0.5 nm程度の空乏層ができます」としているが、0.3〜0.5 nm はポリシリコン空乏層の物理的な厚さではなく、空乏層が実効的に加える SiO2 換算膜厚(EOT/CET の増分)の値。物理的な空乏層幅は約1〜1.5 nm。加えて繁体字訳では正解の選択肢が「等同於實際的閘極絕緣膜變厚」(実際の=物理的な絶縁膜が厚くなる)になっており、「実効的な」の意味が逆転して正解の文が誤りになっている。オランダ語訳は「1 nm台」を「enkele nm」(数nm)としている。
mosfet-022.basis: ポリ空乏層幅 Wd = Qs/(q·Npoly)。Eox≈5 MV/cm(1.5 nm で約0.75 V)なら Qs = εox·Eox ≈ 3.45e-13 F/cm × 5e6 V/cm ≈ 1.7e-6 C/cm²、Npoly = 1e20 cm^-3 で Wd ≈ 1.7e-6/(1.6e-19×1e20) ≈ 1.1 nm。SiO2 換算では εox/εSi ≈ 1/3 を掛けて約0.35 nm。教科書(Taur & Ning 等)でもポリ空乏化は「電気的膜厚を約0.3〜0.5 nm 増やす」と書かれており、0.3〜0.5 nm は換算膜厚の増分である。mosfet-048 の量子効果(SiO2換算で0.3〜0.4 nm)と同じ書き方にそろえるのが正確。zh-hant の「實際的」は actual の意味で、問題の主旨(実効的に厚くなったのと同じ)と逆。
mosfet-022.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

mosfet-048.summary: 解説が CET を「物理膜厚より大きい電気的膜厚」としている。CET が必ず上回るのは EOT(SiO2換算膜厚)で、物理膜厚ではない。High-k 膜では物理膜厚のほうが CET より厚い(例: HfO2 3 nm で EOT 約0.5 nm)。同じ文の後半で EOT に触れており、比べる相手は EOT が正しい。
mosfet-048.basis: 量子効果とポリ空乏化はどちらも絶縁膜「以外」の部分に直列容量を足すので、CET = EOT + Δ(量子効果) + Δ(ポリ空乏化) となり、CET > EOT。SiO2 単層なら物理膜厚 = EOT なので元の書き方でも成り立つが、High-k では物理膜厚 > CET となり誤り。用語集(zh-hant の該当項目)も「CET は EOT より大きい」と書いている。英訳はすでに「exceed the physical EOT」と EOT を比較対象にしている(表現を整えるだけ)。オランダ語の「elektrische diktes」(複数形)も合わせて直す。
mosfet-048.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

wafer-031.summary: The explanation says that wafer diameters became formal metric standards 'from 150 mm onward' (150 mm以降はメートル法の直径が正式な規格). The metric series already starts at 100 mm: the '4-inch' wafer is specified as 100 mm (not 101.6 mm) and the '5-inch' as 125 mm (not 127 mm). Only the 2-inch (50.8 mm) and 3-inch (76.2 mm) sizes are true inch dimensions. The answer key does not change.
wafer-031.basis: SEMI M1 polished-wafer dimensions: 2-inch = 50.8 mm and 3-inch = 76.2 mm (inch-based), then 100 mm, 125 mm, 150 mm, 200 mm, 300 mm (metric). 4 in = 101.6 mm and 5 in = 127 mm, which differ from the 100 mm and 125 mm standards, so those sizes are already metric. Fix changes only '150' to '100' in that sentence in all seven languages; the 150 mm = 6-inch statement earlier in the text is untouched.
wafer-031.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

package-001.summary: The explanation lists gold, copper and aluminum wire, then states without qualification that bonding is done while heating to about 150-200 °C with pressure and ultrasound. That is thermosonic bonding, used for Au/Cu ball bonding. Aluminum wire is normally wedge-bonded ultrasonically at room temperature.
package-001.basis: Thermosonic ball bonding (Au, Cu) uses a heated stage at about 150-200 °C. Ultrasonic wedge bonding of Al wire, both fine Al wire and the thick Al wire used in power modules, is generally done at room temperature. The site itself (package-024) says wedge bonding is common with aluminum wire. As written, the heating condition is stated as true for every wire material listed.
package-001.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

package-038.summary: zh-hant translates 切りしろ (kerf, the material width removed by the cut) as 切割道, which in Taiwanese semiconductor usage means the scribe line or dicing street between dies. The text then says the 'street is nearly zero' for stealth dicing and that blades 'need a street of tens of µm'. That is a different quantity.

memory-hierarchy-030.summary: 独訳で「10万倍」を「100,000-fach」と書いており(選択肢2と解説)、ドイツ語では小数点のコンマとして「100,0倍=100倍」と読めるため、正解の「十〜百倍」と区別できなくなる。また「数十〜100倍」「数十〜100 ns」を「Zehn- bis Hundertfache」「zehn bis 100 ns」(10〜100)と訳しており、下限が「数十」から「10」に変わっている。
memory-hierarchy-030.basis: ガイドラインでは独・蘭・仏の桁区切りは「1.000」「1 000」で、「3,000」のような書き方はしない。100,000 は独語で 100 と読める。範囲は日本語の「数十」(英訳 tens、蘭訳 tientallen、仏訳 quelques dizaines)に合わせる。L1約1 nsに対しDRAM数十〜100 nsなので、比は数十〜100倍。

memory-hierarchy-030.summary: 蘭訳の解説で「10万倍以上」を「Meer dan 100,000 keer」と書いており、オランダ語では「100,0倍=100倍以上」と読める(選択肢は正しく「100.000」)。
memory-hierarchy-030.basis: オランダ語ではコンマが小数点で、桁区切りは「100.000」。「100倍以上」と読めると、正解(数十〜100倍)の説明と食い違い、選択肢2の値とも一致しない。

wafer-030.summary: The explanation says SiC boule growth at 0.1–1 mm per hour is 'a hundredth of silicon's rate or less' (シリコンの100分の1以下). Measured against the silicon pull rate this site gives (wafer-001 and the CZ glossary entry: 'a few cm per hour'), 1 mm/h is only 1/30 to 1/60 of silicon's rate, so the claim does not hold for the upper end of the stated range. The answer key does not change.
wafer-030.basis: Checked with Python: CZ pull rate for 300 mm crystals is about 0.4–1 mm/min = 24–60 mm/h ('数cm/h' in wafer-001). 30/1 = 30 and 60/1 = 60, so 1 mm/h SiC is 1/30–1/60 of silicon; 0.1 mm/h is 1/300–1/600. The stated SiC range therefore spans 'several tens to several hundreds of times slower', not 'below 1/100'. The power-category glossary entry SiC(炭化ケイ素) gives the same 0.1–1 mm/h without the 1/100 claim. Fix replaces only the ratio phrase in all languages; numbers 0.1–1 mm are unchanged.
wafer-030.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

mosfet-026.summary: 解説が「DRAMやフラッシュが電荷を保持できるのも、この絶縁ゲートのおかげです」としている。フラッシュ(浮遊ゲート/電荷トラップ)は絶縁膜に囲まれた電荷保持なので正しいが、1T1C の DRAM はセルキャパシタに電荷をためており、それがアクセストランジスタのソース/ドレインにつながっている。保持を決めるのはオフ時のリーク(接合リーク・サブスレッショルドリーク・GIDL)で、絶縁ゲートではない。
mosfet-026.basis: DRAM の蓄積ノードはアクセストランジスタのゲートではなく拡散層に接続されている。同じカテゴリの mosfet-025 は「DRAMのセルトランジスタ」で GIDL(ドレイン側のリーク)が問題になると書き、mosfet-036 は DRAM セルトランジスタで電流の向きが入れ替わる(チャネルを通って電荷が出入りする)と書いており、026 の「絶縁ゲートのおかげ」という説明とかみ合わない。DRAM を外し、フラッシュだけを例にする。
mosfet-026.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

mosfet-049.basis: ro ≈ 1/(λ·ID)。λ ∝ 1/L なので、ID 一定なら L を2倍で ro は2倍。ところが VGS(と W)を同じにしたまま L を2倍にすると、2乗則で ID も 1/2 になり ro は約4倍になる。どちらで比べるかで値が変わるので「同じドレイン電流なら」を付ける。

reliability-013.summary: The explanation says the strength of the Weibull distribution is that it can represent all three bathtub periods with one (1つの) distribution. A single Weibull distribution (one m) has a hazard rate λ(t) = (m/η)(t/η)^(m−1) that only decreases (m<1), stays constant (m=1) or only increases (m>1). It cannot produce the falling-flat-rising bathtub shape on its own.
reliability-013.basis: The correct statement is the one the question stem makes: depending on the value of the shape parameter, the same distribution family can represent each failure type. The whole bathtub curve needs a combination of Weibull distributions with different m, as a mixture or competing risks. As worded, the sentence suggests that one fitted Weibull covers the whole life. The glossary entry ワイブル分布 (section 形状パラメータと故障の型: 「1つの分布でバスタブ曲線の3つの期間を表せる」) has the same wording and should be fixed in the same way. That is outside this question set and is not included here.
reliability-013.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

reliability-014.summary: The explanation attributes the 150–250 °C peak of stress migration only to atoms being mobile (原子が動きやすい中程度の温度). That reasoning would predict the effect growing steadily with temperature. The peak at an intermediate temperature comes from two competing factors: diffusion speeds up with temperature, while the thermal-mismatch tensile stress falls as the temperature approaches the deposition or anneal (stress-free) temperature. The EN text already says "where atoms are mobile yet stress remains high", so JA and EN also differ. Separately, the nl question says "door spanning in de bedrading". In Dutch "spanning" reads first as electrical voltage, so the stem can be read as "atoms move due to voltage, without current", which points toward an electrical effect. It should say mechanical stress.
reliability-014.basis: Stress migration voiding rate ∝ (stress driving force) × (diffusivity). deposition-011.summary: The explanation attributes the good step coverage of TEOS oxide to TEOS "decomposing easily on the surface" (表面で分解しやすく回り込みがよい). The mechanism is the opposite: TEOS is comparatively unreactive (it needs ~700 °C thermally vs ~400 °C for SiH4/O2), and conformality comes from reactive intermediates with a LOW sticking probability that bounce many times and reach trench sidewalls/bottoms before reacting. A species that reacts readily on first contact gives poor, overhanging coverage.
deposition-011.basis: Contradicts the site glossary entry TEOS ("段差被覆性がよい理由": 反応性の中間体は付着確率が低いため、反応するまでに何度も跳ね返ってトレンチの側壁や底まで届きます; FAQ: 付着確率の低い中間体による表面反応で形成されるため、よりコンフォーマル) and the step-coverage logic of deposition-016 (slow surface reaction -> conformal). High reactivity / high sticking coefficient is what makes silane-based oxide non-conformal. Fix keeps sentence structure and all numbers; only the causal clause is replaced.
deposition-011.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

deposition-033.summary: States that for both sputtering and evaporation the mean free path must be longer than the equipment dimensions. That holds for evaporation (~10⁻⁴ Pa) but not for ordinary magnetron sputtering, which runs at 0.1–1 Pa (as deposition-015 itself says), where the mean free path is only millimetres to centimetres, i.e. comparable to or shorter than the target-to-wafer distance; sputtered atoms do undergo some gas collisions.
deposition-033.basis: λ = kT/(√2·π·d²·p). For Ar at 300 K (d ≈ 0.36 nm): λ ≈ 7 mm at 1 Pa and ≈ 7 cm at 0.1 Pa (glossary 真空蒸着 rightly says only that at ~1e-4 Pa the MFP is far longer than the source-substrate distance). Conventional target-wafer spacing is ~5 cm or more, so the "MFP > chamber size" condition is true only for evaporation (and long-throw sputtering at the low end). Fix keeps the point (vacuum reduces collisions) and gives the correct condition per method, using the 0.1–1 Pa range already used in deposition-015 and the glossary.
deposition-033.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

physics-007.summary: The explanation says that with more electrons the holes decrease "by that amount" (その分だけ; nl "met evenveel" = by the same amount, fr "d'autant", ko "그만큼"), which reads as an equal absolute decrease. Under n·p = ni² the hole density falls in inverse proportion to n (1e16 donors remove only ~1e10 holes, not 1e16). It also states n·p = ni² holds for any doping without the non-degeneracy condition that physics-018 itself gives (it fails in degenerate semiconductors).
physics-007.basis: p = ni²/n: raising n from 1e10 to 1e16 lowers p from 1e10 to 1e4, i.e. by a factor 1e6, not by the same amount. physics-018 and the 縮退半導体/真性キャリア密度 glossary entries say n·p = ni² no longer holds at degenerate doping (Boltzmann approximation and bandgap narrowing), so the "even with doping" statement needs that condition.
physics-007.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

physics-027.summary: States without condition that MOSFET current decreases at high temperature mainly because of the mobility drop. This holds only at high gate overdrive; near threshold the threshold-voltage decrease (about −1 to −2 mV/°C) dominates and the current rises with temperature (zero-temperature-coefficient point, and temperature inversion at low supply voltage). This contradicts mosfet-028, which explicitly says the current drops only at high gate voltage and rises at low gate voltage.
physics-027.basis: ID ∝ μ(T)·(VGS − Vth(T))^α: μ falls with T while Vth also falls, so dID/dT < 0 only when VGS − Vth is large. mosfet-028: 「高ゲート電圧では移動度低下が勝って電流が減り、低ゲート電圧ではVth低下が勝ってリークが増えます」. The glossary 移動度 entry correctly limits the claim to 駆動電流.
physics-027.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

physics-029.summary: Gives the resistivity of intrinsic silicon as about 2×10⁵ Ω·cm. The compare pages say "10⁵ Ω·cm台", which is consistent with either value.
physics-029.basis: 1/(1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 1×10¹⁰ × 1850) = 3.4×10⁵ Ω·cm. With ni = 1.45×10¹⁰ and μ = 1350 + 480: 2.4×10⁵ Ω·cm. Sze (3rd ed., ni = 9.65×10⁹) lists 3.2×10⁵ Ω·cm. A range of 2–3×10⁵ covers the literature and the site's own numbers. Minimal change: widen to a range.

pn-junction-004.summary: The explanation writes I = Is{exp(qV/nkT) − 1} with the ideality factor n, then states unconditionally that current rises tenfold per ~60 mV. That holds only for n = 1; in general it is n × 60 mV per decade (as pn-junction-039, pn-junction-048 and the glossary 理想係数 say). German translation additionally inverts the Ohm's-law sentence ('folgt er wie ein Widerstand nicht dem Ohmschen Gesetz' = 'like a resistor, it does not obey Ohm's law').
pn-junction-004.basis: ΔV per decade = n·(kT/q)·ln10 ≈ n × 59.5 mV at 300 K; real Si diodes have n ≈ 1-2, i.e. 60-120 mV/decade. The condition n = 1 is missing (missing-condition error). DE: placing 'wie ein Widerstand' before 'nicht' makes the resistor the subject of the negation; it must read 'nicht wie ein Widerstand'.
pn-junction-004.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

logic-018.summary: The explanation says Moore outputs 'come directly from the state register' and are therefore low-glitch (EN goes further: 'glitch-free'). In general a Moore output is a combinational function of the state (output-decoding logic between the state register and the output), which can glitch when several state bits change; outputs come directly from the register only when the state is encoded that way. The correct reason Moore outputs are stable is that they change only after a clock edge and input changes/glitches do not propagate to them. The glossary entry ミーリ型 itself says glitch-free Moore outputs require encoding the state so outputs are taken directly from state-register bits.
logic-018.basis: Moore: output = λ(state). With binary state encoding, λ is decoded by gates from multiple flip-flop outputs that toggle at slightly different times, so a decoded output can glitch (standard textbook point; remedies are output-encoded/one-hot states or registered outputs). glossary ミーリ型 (about[1]): 「出力を状態レジスタのビットから直接取り出せるように状態を符号化すれば、出力のグリッチもなくせます」 — i.e. not automatic. Fix keeps the comparison (Moore insulated from input changes, changes only after the edge) and removes the false 'directly from register / glitch-free' premise. Answer unchanged.
logic-018.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)

compiler-046.summary: The last sentence says results may change only when the user explicitly opts in (for example by allowing floating-point reordering). That overstates the rule. The C standard itself lets a floating expression be contracted (C11 6.5p8, FP_CONTRACT), so a * b + c may become one fused multiply-add with a single rounding, and the result can differ from separate multiply and add. GCC does this by default in its GNU C modes (-ffp-contract=fast), and Clang contracts within an expression by default. No explicit user choice is needed. The site's own compiler-047 presents turning a * b + c into one FMA instruction as ordinary instruction selection, which contradicts the 'only when the user explicitly opts in' wording. The same wording appears in every language.
compiler-046.basis: I checked this against C11 6.5p8 (contraction of floating expressions is permitted; whether FP_CONTRACT defaults to on is implementation-defined) and against the documented GCC default of -ffp-contract=fast when not in strict ISO mode. FMA rounds once, so contracting a*b+c can change the last bits. The answer key (choice 2: do not change visible results of a correct program) is still correct, because the language rules define which results count as correct. The fix only widens the last sentence to 'within what the language standard or the chosen settings allow' and keeps the user-option example. No numbers are involved.

compound-008.summary: ja 「GaNは高温・高圧でも分解しやすく融液から結晶を引き上げられない」(zh/ko/de/nl/fr も同じ「高温・高圧でも分解しやすい」) says GaN decomposes easily even under high pressure. That is the wrong way round: nitrogen pressure is what suppresses decomposition, and GaN does melt congruently, but only at about 6 GPa and about 2200 °C. That pressure is impractical for industrial melt growth, so the real reason is that GaN decomposes before it melts at any practical pressure. en already says this correctly ("GaN decomposes before melting").
compound-008.basis: Utsumi et al., Nature Materials 2 (2003) 735, "Congruent melting of gallium nitride at 6 GPa": GaN melts congruently at about 2220 °C and 6 GPa, and below that N2 pressure it decomposes into Ga + N2 before melting. High-pressure solution growth (HNPS, about 1 to 2 GPa) also relies on pressure to stabilize GaN, so "decomposes easily even at high pressure" is wrong. The answer key (foreign substrates) is unchanged. The fix keeps the en meaning; it adds no new glossary links (checked with linkTerms for each language, skipIn(compound)), and de/nl/fr use "6 GPa", which has no decimal-separator issue.

wafer-033.summary: The explanation states without condition that placing square chips on a round wafer wastes 'a few percent' at the edge (外周に数%の無駄). That is true only for small dies. With the gross-die formula, a 100 mm² die on a 300 mm wafer already loses about 9% and a 400–600 mm² die loses about 19–23% (before edge exclusion). advanced-packaging-052 also says the edge loss grows with die size. The answer key does not change.
wafer-033.basis: Gross die per wafer N = πd²/(4S) − πd/√(2S), with d = 300 mm, recomputed in Python. The lost area fraction is 1 − N·S/(πd²/4) = 2√2·√S/d. S = 10 mm² gives 3.0%, 25 → 4.7%, 100 → 9.4% (640 dies), 200 → 13.3%, 400 → 18.9%, 600 → 23.1%. 'A few percent' therefore holds only below about 25–50 mm². Fix gives the range and its dependence on die size in all languages. The choiceNotes ('a square substrate would waste less') stay consistent.
wafer-033.by: AI の点検(2回目の全問点検。指摘の根拠を保守担当が確認)
